001.description: A playful, dramatized interview with fictional correspondent Dr. Rowan Field on crowdsourced moral preferences for autonomous vehicles, and why a preference distribution is not a decision procedure.
001.title: Should the Crowd Program the Car?

002.description: A playful, dramatized interview with fictional correspondent Dr. Rowan Field on what it takes to turn crowdsourced moral preferences into a machine that actually decides: a utility model fit to human judgements, a voting rule that aggregates them, and the gap between an aggregate that can be computed and one that can only be estimated.
002.title: Building the Decider

003.description: A playful, dramatized interview with fictional correspondent Dr. Rowan Field on who the public blames when a human driver and an automated system both make mistakes — and why that blame pattern may quietly weaken the liability pressure meant to force safer designs.
003.title: Who Gets Blamed When Both Are Wrong
